Oversized Camping Chair Heavy Duty Padded Support 400LBS Folding with Cooler Cup Holders Removable Pillow Lumbar Support Pocket Portable for Adults Heavy People Outdoor, Camping, Travel My wife and I wanted to get “taller” chairs for the park, beach, or other needs, not replacing, but complimenting our beach chairs - that are really low to the ground. To that end, when I had the chance to try this Oversized Camping Chair Heavy Duty Padded Support 400LBS, I grabbed it. This chair is a good one, one of the most comfortable either of us has tried, and will be good for our needs. While we have the others, those being so low, can be hard to get up out of and while can be comfortable for awhile, can grow painful. This Oversized Camping Chair Heavy Duty Padded Support 400LBS is not only taller - taking away the need for crawling in and out - it is actually very comfortable. There is a thickness, a padding to the seat and back we are not familiar with in other similar chairs - this alone makes it really nice. There is also a strap system that lets one adjust the lower back support - something that does help in keeping the back from growing tired and helps with comfort. That said, it’s not ‘Perfect,” but far beyond what we have experienced in other such chairs. The chair is overall a decent weight - not so heavy it can’t be carried, but heavy enough for sturdiness and lessen the chance of it tipping over. But also not so heavy you can’t carry it a good distance, but heavy enough one might find relief in having a cart to carry it in. There are plenty of places to hide or store things. There is a side bag that is lined for keeping things cold - that’s cool in and of itself. There is a netting where one can store things like heys. And there is a cup holder. There are plenty of spots, all well placed. Just for the fun of it, my favorite is the cooler bag. The Oversized Camping Chair Heavy Duty Padded Support 400LBS comes with a carrying bag for making things easier, though we found that you need two people to get it in and out the easiest - it is doable with one, but it takes far more effort. And it’s very easy to put down or up - open or closed. I mean, really easy, like most chairs of this style. My wife and I are slightly different heights, my height being a little less, and while I can easily sit in the chair, the cross bards in front are a bit much after say, 30 minutes. That is NOT to say it becomes so uncomfortable I’d have to move, but I’d likely move. For my wife at 5’ 7” she is comfortable and can for longer. We both tried it with a small stool and that, having my legs up, did feel better.

In the end it’s a good chair and we are both happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: Oversized Camping Chair Heavy Duty Padded Support 400LBS Folding with Cooler Cup Holders Removable Pillow Lumbar Support Pocket Portable for Adults Heavy People Outdoor, Camping, Travel

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Montana Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Family Tent with Included Rainfly, Carry Bag, and Spacious Interior, Fits Multiple Queen Airbeds and Sets Up in 15 Minutes As an adult who has just recently returned to the world of camping (I am a leader in my son's cub scout pack), I looked at LOTS of tent options before choosing the Coleman Montana 8 person tent. I checked out reviews on Amazon and CampMor, and talked to as many camping enthusiast friends as I could. My first year in scouting, I borrowed a Eureka 2-person tent from our local boy scout troop, which came up to (maybe) my waist, and just barely fit my full-sized air mattress. After struggling to change clothing while lying down (I could barely kneel, let alone stand), and suffering through a fairly sleepless/stuffy night in the Eureka tent, I decided that the following features were necessary for comfortable camping:

1. The ability to stand up fully. This meant that any tent I chose had to have a center height of at least 72", preferably more (my husband is 6 feet tall, and if I ever want him to join us camping, the tent needs to work for him too. The Montana 8 has a center height of 84" (7 feet).

2. Room for gear and at least two full/queen sized air mattresses. Although the Montana 8 states that there's room for 8 people, the diagram shows these 8 people sleeping in mummy bags very close together. From a comfort perspective, this tent will hold 4-5 people (and their gear) at a maximum, without feeling overly crowded. For the three of us, this fits the bill nicely.

3. Intuitive and easy to set up and take down. While I like camping, I am not an avid camper. Finding a tent that can be set up (and taken down) with only help from a 9 year old was key, and this fits the bill nicely.

4. Good cross-ventilation. After sleeping in a stuffy tent once, I didn't want to repeat the experience. Three windows (the two side windows and the door window) can be rolled down to allow for good air flow and ventilation. We rolled the windows down 1/3 of the way, which provided a very comfortable cross-breeze while sleeping.

5. Waterproof with a bathtub floor. Many of the reviewers stated that they had no problems with leaks along the seams without using any waterproofing sealant. After talking with others and reading some recommendations, I used the Kiwi Camp Dry Heavy Duty Water Repellent to spray the seams prior to our first use, as added protection. We had some light rain during the evening, and much heavier rain the next morning, and the inside of the tent stayed bone dry.

6. Quality. I wanted a tent that would stand up to occasional car camping trips, without having to be replaced on a regular basis. Coleman is a recognized brand, and after talking with folks who own Coleman tents and reading the reviews, I was convinced that this tent would be a good one for our family. So far, I'm pleased!

6. Price. Given that we don't do a lot of camping, I didn't want to spend hundreds on a tent. I purchased the Montana 8 in Blue (not the Elite) from Amazon in mid-May 2015, and paid $136.48; a surprisingly low price for this particular tent model/size.

Some nice features that this tent offers (that weren't on my list of must-haves):

1. A port for electrical/extension cords. While this tent does not have electricity, it does include a port near the door that allows campers to run an extension cord into the tent (for use with lanterns, fans, etc.)

2. A covered entry area. I looked at tents that had screened in areas, but opted for this one instead, choosing to have the extra room inside the tent rather than in a screened area. I had two camp chairs outside - in the evening, when it started to rain, I placed the camp chairs under the front rain fly "awning", on either side of the door. Despite the rain, the chairs stayed mostly dry, with only a few drops of water on them.

3. A "D door". This door has a pole that threads around the D curve, and another one at the hinge axis, which means that the door can function as a real door in terms of opening/closing, rather than a door that must be zipped open and closed. While there are Velcro closures around the D curve, we found that to keep insects from getting in we still had to zip it shut. However, we liked the easy entry!

All in all, my family and I are very pleased with our new tent, and look forward to many years of use!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Montana Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Family Tent with Included Rainfly, Carry Bag, and Spacious Interior, Fits Multiple Queen Airbeds and Sets Up in 15 Minutes

Franklin Sports Glomax Darts Light Up Soft Toss Long dark winter days. Cabin fever. Snowed in. No activity. Kids climbing the walls. What to do...

We're all heading into the basement where we have collected fun games over the years, like an air hockey table, Foosball, electronic darts, an electronic basketball hoop....and now our new addition, the light-up lawn darts game. It is a blast in the basement (although we keep a little bit of lighting on). This is so much fun, and really adds a unique game to break up our wintertime boredom.

Here are a few tips that may help you.

1) We put a few streaks of glow-in-the-dark paint on the rings, to brighten them up a bit, and it worked wonderfully. We got this super bright green glow in the dark paint for about $10 here on Amazon and it worked great: [[ASIN:B00BD63C8W Ultra Green V10 Glow in the Dark Paint 1/2Oz]]

2) Don't give a second thought to replacing the batteries. It's easy. I buy all my replacement button batteries from Amazon. In fact, these lawn darts take the LR41 batteries, which you can get 10 of them from Amazon for about $6: [[ASIN:B000AQ7ME6 Maxell Watch Battery Button Cell LR41 AG3 192 Pack of 10 Batteries]]. Or if you want more, you can get 50 of them for about $13-14: [[ASIN:B0057ON2JA 50 Pack Maxell LR41 AG3 192 button cell battery "NEW HOLOGRAM PACKAGE "]] .

3) If you need replacement parts, which is honestly unlikely, as these things are sturdy as heck. And if you need information on replacement parts, you can email: replacementparts@franklinsports.com or you can call 1-781-341-5178.

Thanks for reading my review. I sure hope it helped you.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Glomax Darts Light Up Soft Toss

text_fidelity_a:
12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent Ok, you can decide if I'm either stupid or desperate. One of the biggest problems encountered working in my yard during the summer in Southwest Florida are these insanely aggressive deer flies. They bite hard,even through your shirt, but they seem to particularly like your cheek, neck or lips. They don't stop pestering you until they are either able to feed or you manage to kill them. The best method I have found so far is to patiently wait for one to land on you and then beat the crap out of it. The problem is that I encounter several of them every day.

So I fell for this flypaper on a hat deal, hoping against hope that it would work where other methods have failed. I have used it for four hours every day for five days in a row. The results: NOT ONE DEER FLY CAUGHT! They continue to buzz around me and I continue to impatiently wait for them to settle so that I can kill them, but not even one deer fly even managed to trap itself on the flypaper by accident.

The product headline says "Repellent Strips" but also discloses that it contains no chemicals or odors. If the product has no chemical on it, how does it repel the deer flies? The only way I can see this working is by attaching the strips to a tennis racket and swinging it at the incoming deer flies. At least I'd get some more exercise and maybe kill a few before they can bite me.
text_fidelity_b: 12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent

text_fidelity_a: Omnia Oven. Your oven on the stove top. Ideal solution for boat oven, camp oven, and RV oven. Also known as a wonder pot. We are in our RV for much of the time, and did not want to use up our propane for cooking during the cold months.  The Omnia does not work on an induction stove, but works very well on a gas stove -- no surprise there.  I purchased an electric hot plate to use with the Omnia, and this combination works well.  I have baked muffins, cornbread, cakes, chicken casserole, cinnamon rolls, etc. and been quite pleased with the outcome. When I made a cake, iced it and sprinkled it with colored sprinkles, it looked like a giant donut.  I didn't hear anyone complaining, though!  Really, I couldn't be more pleased with this Omnia oven.  Food does not brown on the top as it would in a regular oven, but that may be because I use a hot plate as opposed to a gas fire -- don't know.  Would I purchase an Omnia again?  Absolutely!!  In fact, I have purchased this twice.  I made the mistake of placing a very hot Omnia on microfiber towels.  The synthetic towels melted to the bottom of the Omnia, and could not be removed. :(  So I learned the hard way to place a hot Omnia on  a silicone pad or 100% cotton toweling. I did purchase the 2-pack silicone liners which makes clean-up a breeze.  I also purchased the rack which keeps the bottom of food from over browning. The paddle part has an outward curve with a slight concave shape on the inside to allow ease when you put the paddle into the water and have a smooth start with stroking. The concave allows you to have more pressure on pushing water and get you moving faster.

I had two concerns about the lock bar.
1. When I opened it and adjusted the length, the lock bar wasn't tight enough. I could easily adjust the length and even slide the handle part out, which means I could lose the other end of the paddle. The way the lock bar is set up, it does not allow me to adjust the tiny in between screw to make it tighter. I took the risk to open the lock bar, and carefully forced it around clockwise 2 times, thankfully it did not snap the plastic and it is secure now (see image).
2. As mentioned, that section is plastic and with wear and tear, it will crack then you will not be able to adjust the length. When that happens, you will just need to drill and put in a screw to secure them together.

Suggestion for the company:
Since the poles are made of some kind of metal, why not make the lock bar area metal as well instead of plastic? Allow us to be able to adjust the screw for tightness will make this 5 stars.

This paddle is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on amazon.

Well, not until I found these bottles nearly 2 years ago at a Walmart. Contigo is my favorite brand now and all my bottles are this type (push to drink and pour into mouth). I used to prefer bottles that you can sip from, but changed my mind when I tried this model of water bottle. The fact that it stays sealed even without the lip on is great because my son is always knocking it over. You can even lock the button you press to drink if you don't want little hands making messes. I love the handle - super easy to carry and you can even hook it onto something like a belt loop because it has a little carabiner hook. I love the size of this bottle as well and now I'm so spoiled that I get frustrated with most other water bottles which generally hold half the amount of water this one does. I always put ice cold water in my bottles and the condensation is minimal, which I cannot say for any other bottle I've tried.

By the way, the last water bottle from Contigo I had (exact same model) broke after about 1.5 years of rigorous use. This was constant use, all day, several times a day, every day of that 1.5 years. The way it broke was that the flap-lid broke off but everything else worked fine. I've dropped this bottle a lot and it's been durable enough to never crack. Yes these cost more than your average water bottle, but honestly, they've saved me a ton of money in the long run because I've not had to replace ever few months like all other water bottles I've used.

text_fidelity_a: Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued] Before making this purchase, I did my homework in reading reviews and trying out several other ellipticals at fitness stores.  Some of them had an awkward stride motion, others were noise, some were too big, and others were too expensive.  The Schwinn 430 has been just perfect for us.  It relatively compact and has a nice smooth motion to the stride.  It did start to squeak a day or two after we bought and assembled it.  However, after I sprayed the track with white lithium lubricant (lift the wheels off the track and let it dry before bringing the wheels back to the track)the squeak has gone away.  It doesn't have a lot of the extra bells and whistles such as an ipod connection or a fan, but those items could be introduced externally.  Also the monitor is a little difficult to read.  None of those factors really matter to me.  It just seems to be a well built, basic, compact elliptical.  Some reviewers also commented that it was difficult to assemble.  I did not find that to be the case.  We put it together in a couple hours one evening.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued]

text_fidelity_a:
AIM Sports Shotgun Shell Bandolier/56 Rounds I own two of these now. Both are fully loaded, one with slugs and the other with OO buck. If something bad happens and I have to react quickly, I can criss-cross the two bandoliers, grab my Remington Mariner, and have two different loads at my fingertips immediately. A total of 112 rounds should give me plenty of firepower to handle most problems without worrying about using up my ammo.

Using two at a time makes sense for two reasons. One is that you know which load is in which bandolier. The other is that the opposing weight of having one over each shoulder helps keep you in balance when shooting. Good shooting is all about balance and confidence.

On the other hand, maybe I should switch to a high capacity .22 long rifle. I could carry a lot more ammo with far less weight. But nothing generates the immediate respect of the sound of a shotgun being racked. Might as well let them know that something serious is on the way. Chances are they'll bug out before they have the pleasure of meeting you.

text_fidelity_a:
Ibera Bicycle Bag PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Bike Panniers (Pair), Includes Rain Cover , Black These are nice looking and well constructed panniers. However, they have a few issues that leave me not fully satisfied.

First, there is not a single hook, loop, strap, or D ring for you to attach anything to. No place to attach a reflector or a tail light, no place to attach bungees, nothing. Seriously? Has whoever designed these every ridden a bike? There's always something you want to attach somewhere. How hard is it to add a few strategically placed D rings and maybe a strap for a clip-on light?

Second, other than the very flat zippered pocket on the top flap, there is not a divider or a pocket anywhere, inside or out. Everything you put in this pannier is just bouncing around with everything else in there. I like to keep my tools, my spare inner tube, a rag, a few wipes and a few zip ties with me at all times. I'd like to keep all these supplies in a pocket separate from my groceries, laptop, .... But no. There's not a pocket anywhere for a road kit. I had to buy ditty bags and put my emergency kit in those, and toss those in the bottom of these bags, where they continue to bounce around with everything else. But at least they bounce around together.

Third, I find these bags unnecessarily difficult to close. There's a bit of elastic at the back of the cover, near the rack, that does not glide smoothly over the body of the bag. Every single time I close these bags, I have to grab the elastic on both sides and pull it into place for a snug fit. It does make the bag look nice and neat when closed, and maybe it helps keep rain out. But it's annoying that I can't just flip the flap over and close the bag. Also, the clips that hold the top flap down are surprisingly finicky. I'm not sure why, but I have to slide the tab into the clip exactly parallel or it won't go in.

Fourth, the bags do not collapse when empty.They ship flat, and I assumed that I could collapse them at least a little bit when they're empty. But no. They ship with rigid pieces of plastic that you slide into very snug slots to give them structure and shape. You do not want to remove these every time you empty the bag and reinsert them when you load the bag. And even if you did remove them, the bag would just flop around loosely - you can't cinch it so it's smaller. So these bags are always the same (generous) size no matter how much or how little you have in them.

Finally, the bag claims to fit most racks. IT DOES NOT. The clips on top probably do fit over a variety of sizes of rack tubes. And the tab that releases the top clips is a really nice touch, and works well. The problem is the bottom clip, the one that keeps the bag from flapping around when you turn. It is a fixed distance from the top clips, and the distance is very short! I saw that before I purchased these, but I thought I'd be able to rotate the clip so it could grab on to one of the tubes going down to the bottom of my rack. WRONG. That clip does not move up or down, and it does not rotate - you can only slide it left and right. So if the bottom tube of your rack isn't exactly 7" from the top tube, the bottom clip won't connect. I had to remove the bottom clip, flip it upside down, then use a 10" bungee to stretch between the bottom tube of my rack and the inverted clip on this bag. It's a reasonably snug fit and it works well enough. But, contrary to its claims, this bag did not fit my rack - I had to jerry-rig it.

I'm keeping the bags, because I do like the quick on-and-off feature. And they're good sized, and they look sharp. But with a few tweaks to the design they could've been perfect. They're not.
text_fidelity_b: Ibera Bicycle Bag PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Bike Panniers (Pair), Includes Rain Cover , Black

Coleman 3000000455 Latern Pump Kit This kit is dog easy the second time around. Unfortunately the second time may be decades away. Hopefully.
I faithfully disassembled my pump from my 45 year old Coleman stove (Bless em! Most of the guys who built the thing are no doubt long gone to their various rewards)....but anyway, I elected to rebuild the old pump which was a mistake. The new cup is designed for the new rod. It does not work on the old one.
On the old rod there is a metal stop that holds the cup. The new cup is different. If you have a super oldie like mine you will take the metal retaining clip off the new pump with needle nosed pliars. Wiggle under the metal clip and wiggle it off. Slide everything off. Put the round metal ring thingy which holds it to the tank on, then the spring. Follow with the NYLON stop ring. Then put the cup on top of that followed by the new round metal spring clip, or the old. That much is the same.
Put it back in the unit. I started it at the bottom and chased it around with my thumbnail until all of the cup was in....then shoved it home. Some people might have elected to put a bit of grease on the cup before installation but I chose the venerable 3-1 oil before...and after.
After all that it worked like a charm. It's quick and simple if you do it right.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman 3000000455 Latern Pump Kit

text_fidelity_a: Stanley GO The Quick Flip GO Bottle 24OZ Glass We have now owned several of these water bottles, as they are a really great size, and we enjoy the flip top feature; however, before purchasing, please know that the plastic lid has a weak point that will break if dropped on basically any surface at all. I was hopeful that I could find replacement lids either on Amazon or on the Stanley website, but, evidently, they do not make replacement lids for these bottles.  I contacted the Stanley company just to make sure that they do not make a replacement lid (I explained that the lids were broken due to drops, and I was hoping to purchase new lids).  I received an email back stating that all Stanley products are covered under a lifetime warrant, and they then asked me to submit pictures and fill out a detailed form, which I did, though, it took me a long time to compile all of the requested information, and I had to resend the email 4 times as their email kept telling me that it was "undeliverable".  A few days later, I received an email saying that my "ticket" had been resolved and closed, but I had never received a response from my original email.  So, I emailed back stating that my issue was not resolved, and I resent all of the information that they had originally requested.  Weeks later, I received an email apologizing for how busy they are and stating that the warranty doesn't cover accidental damage, and that I should look on their website or Amazon for a replacement lid.  So, basically I just wasted a bunch of time submitting useless information that they never needed and never received an answer to my original questions.  So, that's that.  If you buy this water bottle, just know that if it gets dropped at all, the cheap, plastic lid will break, and you will be left with a very nice, but useless water bottle.

Isokinetics Inc. Adjustable Back Exercise Ball Office Chair - Standard or (Exclusive)"Tall Boy" Frame Height - with 52cm Ball - Office size 60mm/2.5" wheels - w/Starter Pump and Ball Measuring Tape Very well designed chair. Very excellent value for people with back problems. At this price point you have to take a flyer with this chair if you have back issues!

My specific back issues allow me to sit in the chair for only a few hours. I let my chiropractor borrow the chair for a few days. Folks in the office either liked it or didn't.

I'm 6 feet. I definitely needed the accessory leg lift kit.

Two small issues:
1) The nuts that keep the metal retainer bar in place dig into fairly soft plastic and the torquing of the chair in use works the nuts loose. I'm always finding a nut on the floor and I have to re-tighten. Need to add a lock washer and firm up the plastic the nut interfaces to.

2) Two wheels come with locking mechanisms. No matter where you put these wheels you end up locking the wheels somehow. A couple Amazon reviewers recommend using the two back wheels, but I still lock one or the other. If you use the back wheels, then if you don't remember to check for locked when you sit down, then when you get up you will knock the chair over backwards since the chair is so light.

I found a workaround to #2. I Took pliers and twisted off the tab that controls the locking mechanism, then used a knife to shave off the locking lever plastic, to make sure shoes, etc. don't snag and lock the wheels. The locking mechanism still works fine, but now I have to use my fingernail to flip the lever. Problem solved!

I would definitely recommend you try this chair!
text_fidelity_b: Isokinetics Inc. Adjustable Back Exercise Ball Office Chair - Standard or (Exclusive)"Tall Boy" Frame Height - with 52cm Ball - Office size 60mm/2.5" wheels - w/Starter Pump and Ball Measuring Tape

text_fidelity_a:
One Wheel Maya Cycle Bicycle Cargo Trailer Update: Trailer frame has rusted at the welds after just two exposures to rain. I live in the Sonora desert where humidity averages just 20% and it rarely rains. I will sell this trailer or donate it to a local coop.

Original Review [now edited]
I had to invest a few hours in prepping this trailer. If you are not mechanically adept you might need a bike shop to prep and attach this trailer but this could also be true with any trailer.

• The fragile plastic bushing where the trailer mates with the fork cracked and split on the very first use ($12+ shipping to replace it on the Maya website.) I made an addition purchase direct within weeks and asked Maya to replace the defective bushing. They merely ignored my request.
• 16” wheel axle arrived with bearings inadequately greased and cones not properly adjusted.
• Without the critical axle brackets and washers you’re out of business so you’ll want spares $19 + shipping)
• Light is visible through seams in the dry bag. Useless. I use a rigid storage tub instead.
• The dark red flag has no reflective quality making it completely useless for nighttime riding. I made an alternate from a neon yellow reflective vest
• Wing nuts are an invitation to tampering or theft. I used common 3/8 x 24 axle nuts with the built-in raised, scored washer
• Manual states: “an additional axle washer (not supplied) must be placed between the rear fork arm and the Maya axle adapters …” . Within 2 miles with the washers in place, the wheel would suddenly shift to jamb against the arm/stay so hard that the bike couldn’t be ridden. Luckily I had a slightly shorter axle
• The selection of high-quality, after-market 16” inch tires and tubes is extremely limited. Extremely. Stout, 1½ inch thorns are common in my area so I added a Mr Tuffy-brand tire insert to the Kenda Kontact urban tire for greatly improved flat protection.
text_fidelity_b: One Wheel Maya Cycle Bicycle Cargo Trailer

text_fidelity_a:
Magicmode Carbon Badminton Racket Set-with 6 Shuttlecocks and 1 Bag We have enjoyed playing badminton in a club setting, but due to Covid, have been unable to get back. So we decided to get a set for ourselves at home - as well as a net - and still be able to play. This set includes: a bag, 2 rackets, and container of 6 shuttlecocks. I would call this a set ideal for families, the backyard, beach, or picnics, but not for someone at the intermediate or advanced play/club play.

This is a great set. We got two nets here on Amazon for different settings, and took this set to our community tennis court.

The Bag: This is a great bag for this set. It allows one to carry both rackets and the tube of included shuttlecocks. That said, it would be a little better if the bag were even an inch longer. These are a tight fit at the current size. Even without the tube, these rackets have to be in essence pushed in in order to fit. But overall it's a great bag, looks great, and makes carrying easy.

The Rackets: These are nice. Again, this price point, these rackets are for family or couples looking for an hour of fun in the backyard, picnic, or on the beach - not a club setting. They have that nice sound when they connect, and they have a great distance on them. Lightweight, there was no fatigue after an hours play.

The Shuttlecocks: This is a great tube - 6 included. They are feathers, so nicer than the plastic kind. They get a nice sail to them. As feather, these will be damaged quickly, but one can continue to play for a good amount of time. We used one for a few games before needing to trade out. Plastic ones, once damaged, tend to need to be changed more quickly - in my experience.

This is a great set and for the right setting and players, perfect. We are happy and happy to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Magicmode Carbon Badminton Racket Set-with 6 Shuttlecocks and 1 Bag

text_fidelity_a:
StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires We loved the Rio Wonder Wheeler concept, but it didn't work so great in practice. When loaded, it was very difficult to pull over the sand. We then looked at higher-priced ones with balloon wheels, knowing that those would work better on soft sand. I convinced my husband to try these wheels on the Wonder Wheeler first. We followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a 36" length - 3/8" diameter steel rod from ACE (couldn't find one at Home Depot) and 4 metal flat washers to fit the rod (which would be used as new axle). We drilled a hole 1/2 inch from both ends using a titanium drill bit (the carbide one we bought was useless). We used 1/2" pvc pipe cut to the width of the new wheels. We inflated the tires to 4 lbs. with an electric pump; removed linch pins from original axle (don't lose these or plastic bushings), removed original big plastic wheels, bushings, and axle.
To assemble with new tires: 1) We inserted new axle; 2) then the original bushings (with end protrusion cut off); 3) then a metal washer; 4) new tire with pvc inserted through center; 5) another washer; and 6) inserted original linch pins through drilled holes (repeat steps 2-6 on other side). It now works like a dream and saved us several hundred dollars since we didn't have to buy a new cart.
text_fidelity_b: StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires

text_fidelity_a: Antique Brass Nautical Ship Sextant Navigation Tool Pirate Marine Instrument Astrolabe Telescope with Wooden Box Two Slighting Telescope J Scott Sexton I lived on a houseboat 24/7 for 3 years - it was an experience very few people have tried and I have to admit it has its ups and downs, but I wouldn't trade the memories for anything!  I got this sextant for ME, to remind me of my time on the houseboat.  It may not have been a blue water boat (able to cross oceans), but it was a boat able to navigate inland waterways.  Many a night I spent sitting out on my "front deck" looking up at the night sky, the boat rocking in the water...it's such a different way of life and I know that sextants are something sailors used to navigate while out to sea.  When I visit my grandchildren, I do like to talk to them about pursuing things or ways of life that may be different than what others tell them to (or feel they should) - I tell them about living on a boat and how many people have done the same in the past and still do and those who cruise the world and keep a sextant similar to this one just in case their electronics fail and they need to go back to how it was done in "ancient" times.  This sextant and its box have been reproduced in a faithful, authentic manner - its gorgeous and I love it!
text_fidelity_b: Antique Brass Nautical Ship Sextant Navigation Tool Pirate Marine Instrument Astrolabe Telescope with Wooden Box Two Slighting Telescope J Scott Sexton

It's very comfortable, and very lightweight. It fits around my waist, and it also fits well over my shoulder. I'm reviewing the blue medium belt, and as I show in my video, then this belt can go as small as you want it to. So, when picking the size, then look mostly at the maximum size.

This belt will fit a lot of different things in the zippered pocket, as long as they're not wider than about an inch. So, it's a perfect storage place for keys, rolled up money, or loose change.

The LED lights are great. There are two full bands of LED lights, and the options are steady light, fast blinking, and slow blinking. They provide high visibility, so you can be seen by traffic when you're running in the dark or dusk. It's also very comfortable to wear, and lightweight enough so that it won't slow you down.

Pros:
+High visibility with the LED lights
+Very comfortable
+Resizes to fit almost any size
+Can be worn around mid waist, low waist, or around your shoulder
+Easy to set flashing or solid lights

Cons:

text_fidelity_a:
MidTen Magnetic Bore Sight, Red or Green Laser Bore Sight Kit Multiple Caliber, Professional Laser Bore Sighter Rifling Scratch Proof, Suitable for Sighting Scopes Hunting Magnetic Connection Works perfectly magnetized to the end of the barrel. This is obviously for scoped weapons as it's diameter is too large for open sights. If you have a scoped pistol this will work for it as well, otherwise you'll want an actual caliber chamber-fitted bore sight IMO.

This is a no-brainer. No adjustments are available for the laser. It either does or doesn't do the job. To test it, simply place it on a flat level surface and roll it back and forth on the flat. The dot should maintain it's position. If it doesn't, return it for a replacement!

Remember, ALL bore sights are simply to get your rifle or pistol on paper at 25 yards without wasting a box or two of ammo trying to achieve the same result. Once there, fire a few rounds at the desired distance, adjusting your scope each time until it's zeroed in at the yardage you desire.

It doesn't matter that this bore sight isn't perfectly centered, as most aren't anyway contrary to popular belief. Even chamber fitted caliber-specific bore sights aren't perfect and you'll still need to fire a few rounds to be sure your actually sighted and zeroed in at the desired yardage. You can center this by hand on the end of the barrel. It doesn't need to be perfect and will be within a half inch or less of barrel center on target anyway.

At today's ammo prices, this will save you enough in ammo costs and time sighting in so that you'll be able to have more ammo for game or target shooting and put you in the field hunting faster than without one. It's "extremely rare" and I stress, "extremely rare" contrary to the claims here and there that a bore sight zeros you in to that 1/2" group at 100 yards. "Extremely rare". Be prepared to finalize your sighting in at 100 yards to zero with a few rounds after you get on paper.

Be knowledgeable and wise about what a bore sight is designed to do and you'll be happy with your purchase. As long as it gets you on paper so you can see your shot on the paper target in your scope or sighting monocular, the rest is up to you!

Only reason many reviewers leave less than a 5 star rating for this bore sight with few exceptions, is because they don't know how to use it or how to sight in a rifle or pistol in the first place. This is the ONLY bore sight you'll ever need to get your scoped firearms on paper for a good starting point. Like I said, the rest is up to you.

It works! If you don't know the exact procedure to zero your scope in, don't be afraid to ask for help.

I wasn't payed or compensated to state my opinion here. The above opinion comes from understanding what these tools are for, a little logic about what your trying to achieve with them, and a lot of experience. Get some if you don't have any and enjoy your firearm and it's accessories to the best they are capable of performing.
text_fidelity_b: MidTen Magnetic Bore Sight, Red or Green Laser Bore Sight Kit Multiple Caliber, Professional Laser Bore Sighter Rifling Scratch Proof, Suitable for Sighting Scopes Hunting Magnetic Connection

text_fidelity_a:
Fort Knox FTK-PB Pistol Box Handgun Safe I read so many raving reviews about this Fort Knox safe that I waited for months for them to come back into stock (the entire internet was sold out!). Once they finally came back onto Amazon ("The Safe Place" was the vendor), I immediately bought one. Upon examination, the safe itself was very well built. Quality metal and extremely sturdy. Then it came time to program the combination.... Oh my, what a mess. As others have stated, the combination is kind of difficult to figure out. You need to completely unscrew and remove the lock from the safe to reprogram it, which is a mess because it's underneath a layer of foam padding totally covered in glue (which gets EVERYWHERE).

The problem for me started once I did manage to get the combination reset and put back into the safe. For whatever reason, although the combination part of the lock was functioning fine, the actual unlocking mechanism on the safe kept failing. What this resulted in was the combination working (click!), but the safe failing to unlock. Humorously enough, while I was packing the safe back up to return it, it spontaneously burst open when I turned it on its side. Thinking perhaps it had fixed itself, I tried relocking it and reentering the combination. "Click!"...... Stuck locked again....

So, it did end up going back. Unfortunately, the vendor wouldn't pay return shipping on it, and this thing is HEAVY, thus it cost a fortune to ship it back. This thing ended up costing me a whole lot of time, effort, and money, and I'm glad it's gone. With so many positive reviews, I have to believe that I may have just received a lemon. The vendor offered to exchange it for me, but I was too nervous to lock valuables inside of even a new one, with the fear lurking inside me that whatever I put in there may stay there for good. I am giving it two stars though, because even though it didn't work, the build was very impressive, and had it worked, I would have loved it.
text_fidelity_b: Fort Knox FTK-PB Pistol Box Handgun Safe

Tasline Elite Pure Spectra Solid 8X Strand Braided High Power Premium Fishing Line Picture shown is 40lb on a Tranx 401HG

I have been buying from Australia and dealing with the shipping cost and time to get here, so very happy to see it here in Amazon.

This is an excellent braid. Over the years I have spent thousands and thousands of dollars on fishing braid trying to find that "one". If I don't like a braid after one or two sessions, I will pull it all off my reel and throw it in the garbage. I don't like lines that have dyes that bleed off. I also don't like lines that depend on coatings on them as they can have a waxy feel to them, which I feel affects the casting. Some coated lines also take time to break in, and some coatings eventually just wear off. This is one of the many things that makes Tasline so different. They don't use any dyes or coatings. So there is nothing to break in, wear off, or bleed.

Due to the diameter to breaking strain ratio of this braid, and I am able to get more line on my reel. I recently just spooled up 1000m of 20lb braid on my Tern 400. Tasline 20lb has a PE rating of 1.7 and breaks at 34lb which is absolutely perfect for slow pitch jigging setups.

Casting is phenomenal. I think that the 8 strand braids in general are just smoother than the more common 4 strand braids. This line is very quiet going through the guides, and knot retention is excellent.

*Each spool has a hand written number on the back which correlates with breaking strain testing data for that specific spool. My testing has shown that these numbers are accurate and true.

text_fidelity_a: Gaiam Wellbeing Hand Strength Grip I'm a woman, and I wear large gloves due to my long fingers. The pictures all show this ring in a man's hand, so I didn't realize how big it'd be in my hand. When I'm gripping the ring ready to flex it, it reaches from my palm to my fingers with the end joints of my fingers just on top. So I'm trying to bend this ring with the tips of my fingers, which really stresses my tendons. My mom, who has "medium glove" sized hands, could also barely flex the ring in part due to how big the ring was in her hand. I'd either recommend that women try this ring in person before buying it or avoid it. However, I asked two men to try it, and they had no problem with the size and could use it as intended. Both men had men's "large glove" sized hands. Everyone thought it was harder to flex than "medium" would suggest, though. It probably wouldn't work as a physical therapy device for someone recovering from an injury. I was hoping to use it to strengthen my weak hand from a long-ago injury, but I couldn't even use it in my good hand. This ring is 3.5" across at it's widest point and about 13/16" thick.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Wellbeing Hand Strength Grip
